catalysts.headline: Turbo Energy proposed an all-share acquisition of IM2 Energia Solar and Greentech Solutions from its majority shareholder, Umbrella Global Energy, for an aggregate issue amount of EUR 9.271 million; no cash changes hands. IM2 handles solar project development/engineering/construction and Greentech handles O&M; both would become wholly owned subsidiaries. This is a related-party transaction since Umbrella controls both targets.
catalysts.impact: Would extend Turbo Energy from storage/energy-management software into project delivery and lifecycle services; deal provides no disclosed revenue, earnings, cash flow, debt, or margin figures for the targets.

catalysts.headline: Proposed an all-share acquisition of IM2 Energía Solar and Greentech Solutions from majority shareholder Umbrella Global Energy, S.A., issuing 39,501,491 new Turbo Energy ordinary shares (stated issue amount EUR9.271M); would lift Umbrella's stake to ~76.48%. Subject to approval at Turbo Energy's Extraordinary General Meeting set for 2026-12-14, plus approval by both target companies' shareholders.
Launched a project to tokenize financing for hybrid renewable-energy installations with Taurus and the Stellar Development Foundation
catalysts.impact: Shares reportedly ~19% higher in premarket trading

catalysts.headline: Announced a Phase II expansion of the Pamesa Net Zero industrial program: additional orders worth ~EUR6.83M (~$7.6M), adding a net 51 MWh of battery storage across two new industrial sites plus existing locations; equipment deliveries set for H1 2027. Company also cites a $53M industrial backlog across 10 manufacturing sites (366 MWh total capacity).

Turbo Energy brought 62.5 MWh of intelligent battery energy storage online across three industrial sites (ECO Porcelánico, Compacglass, TAU Porcelánico) in the Pamesa Net Zero project; paired with 34 MWp of solar; company says it delivered 130+ MWh to the project in H1 2026

Turbo Energy brought 62.5 MWh of intelligent battery energy storage fully online (installed, commissioned and operating commercially) across three industrial sites in Spain — ECO Porcelánico, Compacglass and TAU Porcelánico — paired with 34 MWp of installed/operating photovoltaic capacity, all part of the company's $53M, 366 MWh Pamesa Net Zero contract (previously disclosed; this is the operational-milestone update, not a new contract)
